paragraphs: RE: PRESENTATION OF ACTUALS FOR 2025 AND ANNUAL BUDGET ESTIMATES FOR THE YEAR 2026 TO THE BOARD OF GOVERNORS MEETING

The 2026 budget has been prepared drawing on the experience and actual performance of the 2025 financial year. All price estimates reflect current market conditions as at the date of preparation, though they remain subject to macroeconomic and behavioral changes.

The school closed 2025 with an enrolment of 2,200 students (1,066 Boarding, 1,134 Day). For 2026, projected enrolment is 2,031 students (1,066 Boarding, 965 Day), reflecting a reduction in day student intake due to space constraints on the school premises.
Income is projected based on 2,031 expected students and current fee rates approved by the Board. Expenditure is based on both historical patterns and prevailing market prices.

The Headteacher proposes a total budget of UGX 10,847,668,577/= (Ten Billion, Eight Hundred Forty-Seven Million, Six Hundred Sixty-Eight Thousand, Five Hundred Seventy-Seven Shillings only) to cater for all recurrent and capital expenditure.
Teachers’ salaries and welfare will continue to be enhanced as a means of motivating staff and sustaining the school’s strong academic performance at both O and A Level.
NOTE: The plans of constructing the boys’ dormitory is under way, pending eviction of squatters from the school land.

Cash and bank balances at 31 December 2025: Centenary A/C 30110308508 (UGX 1,773,011), Centenary A/C 3010001285 (UGX 1,207,113,315), Stanbic A/C 0140007144518 (UGX 1,235,572), Stanbic A/C 0140007144201 (UGX 5,171,619). Total: UGX 1,215,293,517. The Centenary A/C 3010001285 balance is committed for squatter compensation.
Tuition per student per term × 3 terms. O Level: 1,504 students (S.1–S.4). A Level: 527 students (S.5–S.6). 2026 estimate lower due to reduced enrolment.
New S.1 and S.5 students pay UGX 100,000 each (Day and Boarding equalised). O Level: 387 (192 Day + 195 Boarding). A Level: 278 (134 Day + 144 Boarding). Total 665 students. Estimate: UGX 66,500,000.
Collected from all 2,031 students each term unless stated.
All 1,066 boarding students pay UGX 755,400 per term × 3 terms (rate unchanged from 2025). O Level boarders: 771. A Level boarders: 295.
Mandatory government charges passed through the school. 2026 estimate based on 2025 UNEB fees — 2026 circular not yet released.
Tenants in school lock-up units, bus hire, and donations.
New entrants only — 665 students. Rates: O Level Day UGX 395,000, Boarding UGX 465,000; A Level Day UGX 430,000, Boarding UGX 520,000.

Salaries for 48 government-employed staff paid directly by KCCA to their personal accounts. Reduced from 2025 due to retirements not yet replaced. Some of these retired teachers have been retained to provide support as the school corresponds with the Ministry of Education to address the staffing gaps.

Uncollected fees of UGX 254,723,764 from 2025 are budgeted for recovery in 2026. Recovery measures: direct parent contact, reminder letters, and clearance card enforcement at start of each term. These uncollected fees include ugx.90,381,550/= for state house students, who were not verified at an exercise done in March 2026. Also, the 2025 candidates form part of this debt.
Covers expenditure directly relating to teaching quality and examination preparation. Reduction reflects lower 2026 enrolment.
General administration, events, professional services, and compliance. 18% below 2025 approved. Two new lines added: Property Tax and Office Expenses.
All three subscriptions were unbudgeted in 2025 but incurred. Full provision made for 2026.
All BoG, PTA, and staff governance meetings.
Mandatory charges over which the school has no discretion. Must be remitted in full as collected.
Materials for practical and specialist subjects under the new national curriculum.
Supports the school’s objectives to purchase computers, connect labs to internet, and integrate ICT into teaching. 2025 actual was significantly below budget.
Salaries are the single largest operational expenditure. Government salaries are fixed by KCCA; school salaries increase by 3.1% following BoG-approved phased increments.
Covers all student and staff feeding. 24% lower than 2025 approved because Staff Meals (UGX 377,400,000) moved to Staff Welfare vote. Food commodity prices remain a key inflation risk.
Community engagement, student enrichment, institutional visibility, and staff professional growth.
Mass offertory, retreats, vestments, altar wine, hosts, clergy stipends, choir hymn books, and mass instruments.
School drugs, health check-ups, referrals to Nsambya Hospital, and provision for emergencies/epidemics. Reduction proportional to enrolment.
Employer’s statutory 10% NSSF contribution on school-paid staff salaries, remitted monthly to the National Social Security Fund.
Maintaining a hygienic learning environment for students and staff.
Askari training, armed security personnel, uniforms, and security appliances. Reduction reflects a renegotiated security contract.

The 2026 estimate is 42% higher than 2025 approved because Staff Meals (UGX 377,400,000) is introduced as a new line. The Food Basket has been removed from this vote and is now under Kitchen Expenses.
Pens, prep books, markers, glue, files, envelopes, reams of paper, customized books, and plastic identity cards for staff and students.
Vote 21 — Success Party / BoG Scholarships | UGX 79,000,000
Awards for UCE/UACE excellence, end-of-term prizes, departmental awards, and staff performance incentives. 2025 actual was very low due to deferral.
New entrants only — 665 students (S.1 and S.5). O Level estimate higher due to a larger S.1 intake.
Note: Electricity actual in 2025 was only 42% of budget — the YAKA recharge process requires review. NWSC water consistently exceeds budget due to rising tariffs.
The major 2025 capital items (dormitory construction UGX 3.8B, furniture, printer) have been deferred. Only the perimeter wall construction (UGX 35,000,000) is budgeted in 2026.

Compensation of squatters occupying school land — funded from bank loan proceeds in Centenary A/C 3010001285 (UGX 1,207,113,315). This is the single largest development item and requires full Board oversight on every disbursement and the related legal process.

The bank loan taken in 2025 commences repayment in April 2026. The annual instalment of UGX 306,000,000 is a fixed obligation. A standing order should be established with the bank to ensure timely payment.
Outstanding payables at year-end. The 2026 estimate is significantly higher than 2025 (UGX 75,288,415), reflecting anticipated creditors from the squatter compensation programme and capital projects.
St. Peter’s Senior Secondary School — Nsambya  |  Annual Budget Estimates 2026  |  Prepared for Board of Governors
tables: ST. PETER’S SENIOR SECONDARY SCHOOL — NSAMBYA
Maintained quality staff and student welfare throughout the academic year.
Improved student performance at both A and O Level through external facilitators and continuous tests and assessments.
Paid staff salaries and allowances in full and on schedule.
Conducted facilitations for all examination candidates.
Successfully conducted and completed UNEB examinations at both O Level and A Level, including PUJAB application fees for A Level candidates.
Paid for association mock examinations to prepare candidates.
Carried out repairs and general maintenance of the school plant.
Organized co-curricular activities and participated in regional tournaments.
Maintained both student and staff welfare programmes.
Failure by some parents and sponsoring agencies to meet their school fees payment obligations in time, leading to an outstanding debtor balance of UGX 254,723,764.
Fluctuating prices of commodities on the market significantly impacted the cost of food, stationery, and supplies.
High fuel and utilities costs increased operational expenditure, particularly for transport, generator running, and NWSC water bills.
Ensure continuous improvement in academic performance through quality teaching, facilitation, and continuous assessment.
Secure the occupied school land by compensating all squatters — subject to available financing — to protect the school’s physical assets.
Strengthen security by constructing the perimeter wall along Ggaba Road and between the school and the adjacent primary school.
Improve sanitation and health standards across the school premises, including construction of additional toilet facilities.
Improve student and staff welfare, including staff meals, child benefit, transport refund, and house rent allowances.
Stock the school library with new textbooks, reference materials, newspapers, and periodicals.
Top up school salaries for Arts teachers to enhance motivation and retention.
Equip staff with new education technologies through capacity-building workshops (SESEMAT, ACEITEKA, ACP, ASSHU).
Connect the administration block and laboratories to unlimited fibre internet.
Purchase more computers and ICT equipment including projectors to support ICT-integrated teaching.
Setting/marking weekly tests, topical tests, UNEB portal posting.
Internal & external facilitators for O & A Level candidate classes.
Extra-time duties, evening/night prep for boarders.
Examinations set within the school for all classes.
External mocks by senior examiners for candidate classes.
Bereavement support to students, parents, staff, and BoG.
DSTV, Women’s Day, staff parties, public address hire.
HT + 3 Dep. HTs + 2 DOS + Bursar monthly airtime × 12 months.
Hired vehicles for trips; tents/chairs for orientations and celebrations.
Stanbic and Centenary Bank service charges.
External audit and professional advisory services.
Seasonal packages for staff and students.
Legal counsel for land matters and institutional requirements.
Annual taxes on school rental lock-up units.
Meetings and refreshments in the Headteacher’s office.
Official meetings, study tours, and bench-marking visits.
Digital fee collection platform annual subscription.
Digital student performance management and report cards. UGX 3,000,000/term.
Boys’, girls’, and staff common rooms. UGX 2,000,000/term.
Finance, Welfare & Academic, Land committees. Transport and refreshments.
Transport refund for BOT, EOT, HoD, and class teacher meetings.
249 candidates × UGX 315,000. Includes PUJAB application fees.
Technical Drawing, Fine Art, Entrepreneurship materials.
Career guidance, Career Week experts, and orientations.
Lab apparatus, chemicals, specimens for Biology, Chemistry, Physics.
New computers, keyboards, mice for ICT lab expansion.
Fibre internet for admin block and science laboratories.
Replacement toner for office printers and the Riso machine.
5 projectors × UGX 2,000,000 for ICT-integrated classroom teaching.
Servicing and repair of existing computers.
48 government-employed staff. Reduced due to retirements not yet replaced.
Saucepans, plates, stoves, cutlery. Reduction reflects recent procurement.
150 kg beef every Sunday + 200 birds/month. Staff lunch moved to Staff Welfare.
5,900 kg/year. Increase due to market price rises.
222 student bread packs/week + teachers’ break tea.
20,000 kg/term × 3 terms × UGX 6,400/kg. Increase reflects inflation.
Significantly reduced: water infrastructure installed in 2025.
120 × 20L jerrycans/term × 3. Increase due to price inflation.
Fruit days scaled back to twice a month.
Babies’ home, community work, church developments, donations.
Student seminars: leadership, drug abuse, mental health, subject areas, study trips.
School publicity via newspapers, websites, radio, television.
SESEMAT, ACEITEKA, ACP, ASSHU workshops. Includes fees and per diem.
Textbooks, syllabi, question guides for all subjects.
Binding + Bukedde, Daily Monitor, New Vision subscriptions.
Daily newspapers for students and staff.
Water systems, toilets, septic tanks, sewerage repairs.
Buildings, furniture, electricity, beds, general renovations.
Periodic repainting of classrooms, dormitories, and buildings.
9 sessions/year across the entire school compound.
Liquid soap, brooms, squeezers, cleaning agents.
Sanitation tools, bins, janitorial machinery, protective equipment.
Moved to Kitchen Expenses to avoid double-counting.
Daily transport allowance for all staff, 7 days/week, 12 months.
UGX 45,000,000/term × 3. Contribution to staff children’s school fees.
Monthly mileage for HT (UGX 900K) and 3 Dep. HTs (UGX 250K each).
Rent for residential teachers near school for supervision.
Legion of Mary, patriotism, interact, debate clubs.
Balls, nets, jerseys, shoes. Copa Cola leagues and regional tournaments.
Inter-house competitions, costume hire, trainer fees. Restored from very low 2025 actual.
UMEME YAKA recharge. Estimate reduced but realistic.
Office telephones, postal services, and coordination airtime.
Monthly NWSC bills + water trucks. 2025 actual exceeded budget by UGX 20M.
Repairs, servicing, maintenance of school bus and vehicles.
Generator, school bus, and other vehicles.
PMO, Third Party, and related insurance. No payment in 2025; reinstated.
Along Ggaba Road and between school and primary.
Proposed; requires BoG costing and approval.
